subject: general
question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 28% and its height is increased by 141%, then what is the percentage increase (closest integer) in its volume?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a cylinder V ∝ r²h.

Net change in Volume = [ (1 − 0.28)² × (1 + 1.41) ] − 1

Net change = [ 0.72 × 0.72 × 2.41 ] − 1 = 1.249488 − 1 = 0.249488

Percentage increase ≈ 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/055ef8d7c226c34a71e511ca5b72bf4e4d0e90321217c93447a9b636ea051a14.png] 

**Given:**

Decrease in **Radius** (r) = 28% ⇒ Final r = 100 − 28 = 72% of Initial

Increase in **Height** (h) = 141% ⇒ Final h = 100 + 141 = 241% of Initial

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Right Circular Cylinder = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Initial Radius = 100 and Initial Height = 100

⇒ Initial Volume (V₁) = π × (100)² × 100 = 1,000,000π

⇒ New Radius = 72 and New Height = 241

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = π × (72)² × 241

⇒ V₂ = π × 5184 × 241 = 1,249,344π

⇒ Percentage Increase = [ (V₂ − V₁) ÷ V₁ ] × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = [ (1,249,344π − 1,000,000π) ÷ 1,000,000π ] × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = [ 249,344 ÷ 1,000,000 ] × 100 = 24.9344%

⇒ Closest integer value = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

For r², use formula x + y + (xy/100) twice or use the multiplier method for easier calculation when percentages are large.

Surface Area Change

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh. Change in CSA depends on only one power of r and one power of h.

Cylinder Properties

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(h + r). Changes in TSA involve additive terms and do not follow simple product rules.</p
